messages:
ben (customer-success): FYI customer hit a regression after a KMS key rotate on their Private deployment. App calls to decrypt are returning TLS handshake errors and 502s since 09:04 UTC.

maria (support): Can you paste a minimal repro request + error from the app logs? Also which deployment: VPC, on-prem package, and region?

ben (customer-success): Private (VPC) in eu-west-1. Repro curl from their bastion: 
```
curl -v https://kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal/keys/abc/decrypt -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"ciphertext":"..."}'
```
Response: `* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):` then `* SSL: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain` and eventually `curl: (35) SSL connect error`. App logs show `rpc: TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` and intermittently `connect: connection refused`.

maria (support): Thanks. @sylvia can you check if this is an SNI/cert mismatch or an egress block? Those are the two usuals for Private KMS flakiness after rotation.

sylvia (eng-infra): On it. Ask customer to run a couple quick checks from their bastion: `dig +short kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal` and an openssl s_client with SNI: 
```
openssl s_client -connect kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal:443 -servername kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal
```
We need to see cert subject and whether the CN/SAN matches the hostname. If the cert CN is the old cluster name it will fail verification. Also check `tcpdump -n host <kms-ip> and port 443` while curling to see SYN/SYN-ACK.

ben (customer-success): Customer ran those, sent output. `dig` resolves to 10.52.18.73 (private). `openssl` output shows subject `/CN=kms.cluster.internal` and SANs `DNS:kms.cluster.internal` (no entry for `kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal`). Chain otherwise valid. Also tcpdump shows SYN from bastion but no SYN/ACK back.

raj (eng-ml): Certificate CN mismatch explains the verify error. But lack of SYN/ACK indicates network filtering too. Two parallel issues: 1) DNS/name used by client doesn't match certificate CN (SNI issue), 2) outbound traffic to the HSM/KMS appliance is being dropped by customer firewall/egress allowlist.

maria (support): Agreed. For remediation: we should (A) get the client to target the CN/SAN the KMS cert presents or update the KMS cert to include the VPC hostname. (B) ensure egress allowlist and routes permit traffic to the HSM/KMS appliance IPs on the required ports. Ask customer for their egress ACL and NAT/GW config.

sylvia (eng-infra): Additional checks: 
- Check their CoreDNS/cache: if the cluster is still resolving an old VIP (post-rotate) they might be hitting a decommissioned node. TTL flush helps: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=kube-dns` or restart coredns in their environment.
- Verify the TLS client cert is present if the KMS path requires mTLS: `kubectl get secret redwood-kms-client -o yaml` and confirm keys mounted. Missing client certs can show as `tls: bad certificate`.

ben (customer-success): They confirmed they have the client cert secret present. I asked them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.52.18.73:443 -servername kms.cluster.internal` and it succeeded (certificate matched when SNI used as kms.cluster.internal). But when using the customer hostname it fails.

maria (support): So action items for the customer: 
1) Add the KMS/HSM appliance IP(s) 10.52.18.72-10.52.18.75 to their egress allowlist (tcp/443 and tcp/8443 as a precaution).
2) Either update the DNS entry `kms.customer-vpc.redwood.internal` to point to the certificate CN (or vice versa) OR reissue the KMS cert to include the customer hostname in SANs.
3) Flush DNS caches (bastion + kube-dns) or bump TTL.
4) If they have a stateful firewall, ensure return-path NAT is enabled — tcpdump shows SYNs leaving but no replies, suggesting asymmetric routing/backplane block.

raj (eng-ml): For a quick mitigation while they change certs: have the app set `KMS_TLS_SERVER_NAME=kms.cluster.internal` (or equivalent SNI override) so SNI matches certificate, but only if they trust that internal hostname mapping. This avoids changing certs immediately.

ben (customer-success): Customer applied a temporary firewall rule to allow the IP range and added an SNI override in app config. After that, decrypt calls started succeeding (no more TLS errors) and latency returned to normal. They will coordinate with their infra team to add proper SANs on the cert and a permanent allowlist entry.

maria (support): Great — please capture the final state and key logs. Also ask them to enable debug logs for one hour and drop them here with obfuscated tokens so we can close the escalation if nothing else flaps.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0471 (internal tracking) — assigned to eng-infra for postmortem follow-up.

maria (support): Notes for postmortem: root cause = host/SNI mismatch after key rotation combined with egress ACL blocking return traffic (asymmetric routing). Remediation documented above. Recommend we add a KB article for Private KMS rotations: checklist (DNS, SANs, egress IP ranges, SNI overrides, coredns flush).

ben (customer-success): Customer will implement cert SAN fix and permanent allowlist. I'll update when they confirm. Thanks team :thumbsup:
